A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 29-page versions of the same work. Their main text, algorithms, equations, Figures 1–12, Table 1, and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original experiments on LMSYS prompts measuring token overcharging, provider utility and margins, and GPU energy consumption, including the results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v4 retains these original Llama, Gemma, and Ministral experiments, including the energy measurements in Figure 11 and Table 1 and the multilingual analysis in Appendix C.4.

M1.justification: The principal-agent model, token-splitting Algorithms 1–2, plausibility checks, and pay-per-character pricing prescription are unchanged. Algorithm-caption edits only correct wording.

E1.justification: Both versions use LMSYS-Chat-1M prompts for the same token-reporting and pricing tasks, retaining English, Spanish, Russian, and Chinese coverage. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Truthful reporting remains the reference for Algorithm 2's utility gains in Figures 3 and 7. The existing reporting-policy and pricing comparisons are retained; the newly cited auditing work is not evaluated as a comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix A revises the stated GPU setting from A100/Ampere to H100/Hopper. This resolves a conflict with Figure 11 and Table 1, which already specified H100 in v3. Other evaluation settings are retained, and the PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix C retains the same temperature and top-p sensitivity studies, tokenization examples, energy-cost analysis, and language-stratified margins. The spelling correction in Figure 10 does not change the case studied or its findings.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five independent generations with different seeds and symmetric 90% confidence intervals using the same t-distribution value of 2.015 in Appendix A. Statistical reporting in the figures and Table 1 is unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical results and plotted findings are retained. For example, Section 3.3 reports the same Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct overcharging values of 11.2%, 1.8%, and 0.28%, and all Table 1 measurements match. Result-display edits correct labels and spelling.

T1.justification: The definitions, hardness results, incentive-compatibility characterization, and Appendix B proofs are unchanged. Correcting c_0 to c_o in Section 4 standardizes notation without changing mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, five stated contributions, and conclusions retain the same claims about misreporting incentives, computational hardness, profitable plausible retokenization, and character-based pricing. The fifth contribution merely moves onto page 3.

C2.justification: The interpretations and limitations concerning transparency, proprietary models, verbosity, prompt representativeness, and market dynamics remain unchanged. Section 5's existing suggestion of statistical auditing gains a citation without a new substantive argument.

D1.justification: Appendix A corrects the hardware description and replaces a duplicated Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct entry with the already-evaluated Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct. Footnote 3 changes the code repository organization from Networks-Learning to Human-Centric-Machine-Learning.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds Velasco et al. (2026), Auditing pay-per-token in large language models. Other reference edits update or consolidate existing works, including the renamed Chatzi paper with the same arXiv identifier; the broader research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: v4 makes limited grammar, spelling, notation, affiliation, and bibliographic corrections. The section organization and narrative remain intact, with some text reflow across page boundaries.

P2.justification: Figure 7 changes four y-axis labels from 'Increase in profit' to 'Increase in utility'; Table 1 corrects Gemma model suffixes from 'In' to 'It'. Figure 10 corrects a spelling error, and affiliation/reference edits cause limited reflow. No figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly improves reporting accuracy and consistency by resolving the A100/H100 documentation conflict, correcting model names, and aligning Figure 7's labels with the existing utility analysis. The added auditing citation also improves coverage. These are useful refinements to otherwise unchanged methods, proofs, results, and limitations.
